ops.text: The canvas refuses a locked element and toasts “This element is locked. Unlock it in the Layers panel.” (useSelectionBehavior.ts:88,106,134). Half of a three-part defect: UX-H-15 and UX-H-14 belong to the Layers lane and are NOT drawn as fixed here.

why: UX-D-04, UX-D-05, UX-D-06, UX-D-07, UX-D-19 plus the SPEC conflicts — recorded, not silently resolved

ops.name: title/OPEN DECISIONS
ops.text: Inspector · OPEN DECISIONS (V2 → V1) — recorded, not resolved

ops.name: body/decisions
ops.text:
1. PANEL WIDTH — drawn at 300 (--bk-size-inspector), never collapsed. SPEC-INSPECTOR §6 says “No new panel width. 300” and never contemplates being collapsed; SPEC-NAVIGATION proposes that the wide drawer collapses the inspector; SPEC-PUBLISH-PANEL says the expanded state changes “nothing else”. Three specs, one layout, three answers (PHASE4-QA §2.1). V1 already answers it — all 30 panel boards in this section are 300. OPEN, not silently adopted.

2. EXPANDED DRAWER — drawn at 700, which is what LeftSidebar.tsx:586-587 does today. SPEC-NAVIGATION's 560 proposal is filed, not applied (shared brief).

3. AI HOME — SPEC-NAVIGATION §2.5 puts AI IN the inspector column with a “‹ Inspector” way back; SPEC-INSPECTOR §6 says it is docked BESIDE the inspector rather than over it, and calls that an inheritance. Not the same decision, and “beside” needs horizontal room neither spec allocates at 300 (PHASE4-QA §2.2). OPEN. UX-D-01 is only closed by whichever answer wins.

4. “ALL LIKE THIS” SCOPE — either scope the peer set to the active page, and the existing copy becomes true, or keep it project-wide and say so (“also changes 9 buttons on 3 other pages”) with a way to see them first. The peer set is getAllElements() — every registered element across all loaded pages (ElementManager.ts:151-158), cleared only by a full project reset (:530-533) — while the dropdown says “on this page” (ScopeDropdown.tsx:153,159). OPEN (UX-D-04). Either way the reach is a working MODE: it survives a selection change to another element of the same type and ends explicitly, rather than being reset by useEffect([selectedElement?.id]) (ProInspector.tsx:110-114) (UX-D-05).

5. “WHOLE SITE” — leaves the reach dropdown. It is navigation to Brand, has no controls behind it, and renders a takeover card while the pill above still reads “This” (SPEC-INSPECTOR §2.4, UX-D-06). OPEN — a Navigation-lane move, not an Inspector-lane drawing.

6. THE PROPERTIES REGISTRY — 185 definitions across 31 families, exported at config/index.ts:19-22 and imported by nothing. Two acceptable outcomes, no third: make it the source the sections render from, or delete it. Leaving it is what has now cost two audits (UX-D-07). OPEN.

7. LAYERS BREAKPOINT BADGE — NOT drawn as working anywhere in this section. UX-D-19 and UX-H-16 are ONE defect: useLayerTree.ts:88-95 never populates breakpointOverrides, so the T/M badges at LayerTreeItem.tsx:276-281 can never render. It is the Layers lane's to fix; this section only requires that what the inspector hides per breakpoint has an echo somewhere.

8. VISIBILITY KEYS — the section writes --hide-${breakpointId} (VisibilitySection.tsx:36-45) while its registry entry declares display / visibility / opacity / pointer-events (registry/effects.tsx:128-132). The write itself is honoured end to end (Canvas.css:763-767, ExportEngine.ts:126-128), so this is a labelling defect: declare --hide-desktop / tablet / mobile and “applies”, auto-expand and the footer count all describe what the section does (UX-D-18).

9. NOT DRAWN, BY DESIGN — five code fixes this design cannot paper over: composite types need real profiles and “tabs” is not even a key in PROFILE_MAP; FormSettingsSection must be rebuilt on chrome-ui before it can be mounted (it is finished and exported at shared/forms/index.ts:16, mounted nowhere, and its raw <select>/<input> with inline styles fail Gate 24 inside editor/); the peer set is getAllElements(); no forced-state mechanism exists anywhere in the package; the lock is enforced in useSelectionBehavior only. Until they land, the panel cannot tell the truth about what it is editing (SPEC-INSPECTOR §7).
